(Srishti, et al., 2023) further investigates the implementation of AI into the 
education experience, highlighting various tools such as: early warning systems 
for students falling behind, language translation tools, analytics, and data-driven 
decision making. These tools can be used to help optimise the learning 
experience, by enabling teachers to intervene with students falling behind and 
help guide the design and development of the curriculum.  
(Sallam, 2023) discusses the benefits and possible concerns with LLMs within 
the context of health care education. They highlight its ability to create 
customised realistic clinical cases and offer personalised support during self-
learning sessions. Despite this the current state of LLMs are prone to produce 
inaccurate and misleading information that may be subject to bias and 
dishonesty. 
(Bin-Nashwan, et al., 2023) highlights the potential authenticity issues produced 
from creating academic articles and essays using LLM’s such as ChatGPT; 
implying that over usage undermines the educational process of developing 
critical thinking and research skills. This issue is particularly important, and more 
research needs to be conducted on the potential negative educational effects of 
AI usage with children. 
A paper by (Prasain & Bajaj, 2020) investigates how NLPs can be used to mark 
written answers to questions. They express that NLPs, at the time of writing 
(which was a long time ago in terms of AI development), are relatively good at 
marking short answers, however, they tend to struggle at marking longer 
answers such as essays. This less accurate marking could be misleading to 
students.  
Overall, AI seems to be a tool that is and can greatly affect the education sector, 
enabling students to learn independently with increased feedback. It seems
